headline: Approved conditional development plan for mixed-use project at 282 Loudon Rd and nearby lots
summary: The project includes about 600 apartments and 329,200 square feet of commercial and retail space. No construction is allowed yet, but the approval lets subdivision and site plan applications move forward. Final approval depends on a full traffic study and a later public hearing.
decisions: Approved comprehensive development plan for a mixed-use development at Loudon Rd and Sheep Davis Rd lots, 9-0 with conditions.
Accepted the Public Safety Advisory Board master plan report 9-0.
Nominated Planning Board members and others to the 15-member Master Plan Advisory Subcommittee, 9-0.
Nominated Noah Hodgetts, Chris Carley and Elizabeth Immen to the Master Plan Advisory Subcommittee, 9-0.
Agreed by consensus to move forward with a youth event with NH Listens.
Agreed by consensus to hold the six neighborhood forums on a Friday night and a Saturday morning.

City of Concord Planning Board 
November 2, 2026 - Draft 
 Minutes 
 
 
1 
 
 
The regular monthly meeting of the Concord Planning Board was held on November 2, 2026, at 7:00 
p.m., in City Council Chambers at 37 Green St, Concord. 
 
Attendees:   Dina Condodemetraky, David Fox, Matthew Hicks, Teresa Rosenberger (Ex-Officio for 
City Manager), Amanda Savage, Eaton Tarbell, Councilor Brent Todd, Paige Wilber and 
Chair Richard Woodfin 
 
Absent:   Alternate Frank Kenison 
 
Staff: Tim Thompson – (Assistant Director of Community Development / Acting City Planner), 
Alec Bass (Assistant City Planner – Community Planning), Krista Tremblay 
(Administrative Technician III), Mike Bezanson (City Engineer), and Matt Walsh 
(Deputy City Manager – Community Development) 
 
 
The Board will hold a Nonpublic Session under RSA 91-A:3.II(c) at 6p.m. 
 
 
 
1. Call to Order 
Chair Woodfin called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. 
 
2. Roll Call 
The Acting Clerk of the Planning Board, Tim Thompson, did the roll call, noting that a quorum is 
present. 
 
Chair Woodfin noted for the record to seat Alternate Member LaFreniere as a voting member due to 
the absence of Paige Wilber.  
 
On a motion made by Councilor Todd, seconded by Member Condodemetraky, the Planning Board 
voted to enter the non-public session at 6:02 p.m. by roll call vote 8 in favor (Condodemetraky, Fox, 
Hicks, LaFreniere, Savage, Tarbell, Todd and Woodfin) 0 opposed. All in favor. The motion passed 
unanimously. 
 
Paige Wilber arrived at 6:04 p.m. and Chair Woodfin recognized Paige Wilber as regular voting 
member and Alternate Member LaFreniere is no longer a voting member.  
 
Theresa Rosenberger arrived to the meeting at 6:14 p.m. 
 
On a motion made by Councilor Todd, seconded by Member Hicks, the Planning Board voted to exit 
the non-public session at 6:49 p.m. by roll call vote 9 in favor (Condodemetraky, Fox, Hicks, 
Rosenberger, Savage, Tarbell, Todd, Wilber and Woodfin) to 0 opposed. All in favor. The motion 
passed unanimously. 
 
On a motion made by Member Councilor Todd, seconded by Member Fox, the Planning Board made 
a motion at 6:50 p.m. to seal the non-public meeting minutes due to Divulgence of the information

likely would affect adversely the reputation of any person other than a member of the public body 
itself by roll call vote 9 in favor (Condodemetraky, Fox, Hicks, Rosenberger, Savage, Tarbell, Todd, 
Wilber and Woodfin) to 0 opposed. The motion passed unanimously. 
 
3. Agenda Overview 
 
 
4. Site Plan, Subdivision and Conditional Use Permit Applications 
 
4A. Gallagher, Callahan, & Gartrell, PC, Jones and Beach Engineering, Inc, and Onyx Partners, Ltd, on 
behalf of Onyx SteepleGate Concord, LLC, Onyx Regal Concord, LLC, and Onyx TD Concord, 
LLC, requests comprehensive development plan approval for the consolidation of condominium and 
resubdivision into separate lots and ownership, and a proposed mixed-use redevelopment to include 
certain on and offsite improvements, a fueling station, and approximately 600 residential unit 
apartments, approximately 329,200-square-feet of commercial/retail, and approximately 5,040 
square-feet of restaurant use at Tax Maps: 611Z Lot 40 addressed as 270 Loudon Rd; 611Z Lot 39 
addressed as 282 Loudon Rd; 61Z Lot 9 addressed as 277 Sheep Davis Rd 270; and, 611Z Lot 41 
addressed as 260 Loudon Road, all within the Gateway Performance (GWP) District. (2026-041)(PL-
CDP-2026-0002) 
 
Mr. Thompson stated as mentioned at prior meetings, this CDP application is the first step in the 
process to facilitate the redevelopment of the former Steeplegate Mall and Regal Cinema 
sites.  Because the property is located in the Gateway Performance District, a CDP is required by the 
Zoning Ordinance prior to the submission of any subdivision applications.  A CDP itself does not 
allow any actual construction to take place, it simply opens the door to subdivision and site plan 
applications for the redevelopment of the property. In the case of the Onyx project, the developers are 
not proposing a traditional phased implementation of construction, which given the sheer size and 
scale of this redevelopment creates a challenge in getting a comprehensive traffic impact analysis 
completed as part of the CDP whereas in a phased CDP it could be deferred to individual site plan 
applications. Because Onyx is proposing that the development will not follow a phased approach, the 
City and State of NH need to have a complete and comprehensive traffic impact analysis that 
generally indicates necessary off-site improvements and preliminary costs associated with those 
improvements.  This traffic review with the City and the State are still ongoing, and there needs to be 
resolution on it prior to the Board granting a final approval of the CDP.  Typically, staff would not 
recommend the Board grant conditional approval with such a large piece of the puzzle still 
outstanding.  However, in an effort to assist in the redevelopment of this important piece of property, 
staff has developed conditions of approval that we are ultimately comfortable with, such that the CDP 
will need to return to the Board for a compliance public hearing once the City and State have resolved 
the traffic impact issues with the applicant. Based on this approach, staff is recommending the Board 
grant conditional approval to the CDP with the conditions listed in the staff memo. Before I conclude 
my comments, I want to mention that there are now 3 related applications that have been submitted 
by the applicant, the previously continued site plan for the “R3” building containing 110 residential 
units, and recently submitted applications for a subdivision of the mall property, and a site plan for 
the redevelopment of the former Regal Cinemas property.  None of these 3 submitted applications are 
consistent with the CDP application before you tonight.  I want to stress to the applicant that 
consistency with the CDP is essential to an efficient and timely review process for these subsequent
City of Concord Planning Board

3 
 
 
applications.  The City Staff cannot be reasonable expected to be reviewing applications for 
development of these projects without there being consistency with the CDP.  I would urge the 
applicant to consider how these applications have been submitted and if it makes sense to table these 
applications at the November 18 meeting so that the applicant can redesign the applications such that 
they care all consistent with the CDP. 
  
Ari Pollack (214 N Main St, Concord), Doug Richardson (220 Reservoir St Ste 3, Needham MA) and 
Ian MacDermit (85 Portsmouth Ave, Stratham) are present to represent this application. Mr. Pollack 
agrees with Mr. Thompson’s summary. Mr. Pollack stated at this time they are comfortable that the 
CDP reflects their intensions. Mr. Pollack noted there will be instances where it diverges from the 
details of what they have put in front of the Board in form of other applications. If need be they can 
adjust the CDP as the project rolls forward. Mr. Pollack noted this is a master plan for a large 
redevelopment of a parcel. Mr. Pollack stated they are in agreement with the staff recommended 
condition of approval.  
 
Chair Woodfin asked if there are any questions from the Board. Chair Woodfin asked if there are any 
members of the audience that has any questions and there were none.  
 
Member Fox asked about the development of the pond. 
 
Mr. Pollack stated the resources they were installing around the water were not valued by most that 
they encountered. It was more important to see the housing and retail.  
 
Member Condodemetraky asked out of the retail space are they all earmarked. 
 
Mr. Pollack stated the anchors are earmarked and the smaller spaces are still filling. They have a few 
and do not have them all.  
 
Alternate Leon LaFreniere is concerned the Board is being asked to make a decision and there are 
applications pending that are inconsistent. How does the Board reconcile that. Member LaFreniere 
understands it is a living document and subject to change. If there are three applications that are 
inconsistent with this plan and how do they move forward with that.  
 
Mr. Pollack stated one of three things happen. We decide there is not an inconsistency because the 
master plan itself contains a lot of site plan detail that they could have left off and had it work more as 
a concept than a finite document. They might decide some of the detail shown is not important at this 
level or they can make changes to be consistent with the applications that are filed. Mr. Pollack asked 
are they material and how to make sense of them. Mr. Pollack noted they could come back and say 
there are a number of places where the CDP does not reflect our current intentions. Mr. Pollack stated 
they are not overlooking discrepancies. They want to spend some time understanding are they 
material and how best to fix them.  
 
Mr. Thompson stated the R3 building was submitted prior this latest iteration of the CDP. The other 
two applications came in before the determination had been made that we were going down this path 
of a conditional approval for a CDP. Mr. Thompson noted the CDP is only required in this district 
when you are subdividing the property. There is no requirement for site plan.
City of Concord Planning Board 
November 2, 2026 - Draft 
 Minutes 
 
 
4 
 
 
Mr. Pollack stated they are looking to show progress to our partners and potential partners. 
 
Chair Woodfin opened the public hearing, after receiving no public testimony, Chair Woodfin closed 
the public hearing.  
 
Chair Woodfin stated the findings of fact include the information provided in the staff reports; the 
applicant’s submission materials; testimony provided during the public hearing; and/or other 
documents or materials provided in the public hearing.  
 
On a motion made by Member Hicks, seconded by Councilor Todd, the Board voted 9-0-0 to grant 
comprehensive development plan (CDP) approval for the proposed dissolution of existing 
condominium, site consolidation and resubdivision for a mixed-use development at 282 Loudon Rd, 
270 Loudon Rd, 277 Sheep Davis Rd, and 260 Loudon Rd in the Gateway Performance (GWP) 
District, subject to the following precedent and subsequent conditions:  
(a) Precedent Conditions – to be fulfilled within one year and prior to signature of the CDP plat by 
the Chair and Clerk of the Planning Board, unless otherwise specified.  
1. Revise the CDP plat as follows:  
a. Per Section 13.01(8) Impact Studies and 18.03 Submittal Requirements, the applicant 
shall provide overview sheets of all necessary offsite improvements and responsible parties. 
b. Per Section 18.05 Standards for Review (1) Zoning, the plan shall demonstrate that the 
approximate general location of the loading spaces can feasibly be constructed while  
maintaining zoning compliance with Section 28-7-13 Off-Street Loading Requirements and 
Section 20 of the Site Plan Regulations. 
c. Per Section 18.05 Standards for Review (4) Easements and Covenants, the applicant shall 
provide a separate narrative, which clearly provides a summary of existing easements which 
need to remain or be modified for the project. This narrative shall also include a clear 
summary of the proposed easements (access, utility, parking, grading/slope, or other as 
applicable) necessary as part of the CDP for each lot and for all utilities. 
d. Per Section 12.02(1) Title Block (c), the latest CDP plan revision (September 16, 2026) 
shall be added to the revision block of the CDP plan set. 
2. Revise the plan for compliance with the Subdivision Regulations and Construction 
Standards and Details as noted in the attached 8-page memo to Alec Bass from Mike Bezanson, 
Paul Gildersleeve and Pete Kohalmi, dated October 15, 2026. 
3. The plan shall list, describe, and date all approvals, variances, waivers, and conditional 
use permits received. The application shall also be revised to conform with any denials made by 
the Board. 
4. Because the applicant is not proposing any formal phasing of the development 
contemplated by the CDP, all on- and off-site transportation improvements must be constructed 
as part of the initial construction of the project.  The complete and comprehensive traffic impact 
analysis for the entire development program shall be completed as part of this CDP, prior to final 
approval of the CDP by the Chair and Clerk. Further: 
a. Per Section 13.01(8) Impact Studies (c), the applicant shall satisfactorily resolve any 
current (and any forthcoming) traffic comments from NHDOT, the City Engineering 
Division, and City peer review consultant VHB regarding the CDP Traffic Impact analysis 
prepared by VAI.  Satisfactory resolution shall be defined as acceptance of any revisions by
City of Concord Planning Board

 Minutes 
 
 
5 
 
 
the applicant which allow for the identification of, and preliminary cost estimates related to, 
off-site transportation improvements to public (both City and State of NH) roadways, rights-
of-ways, and pedestrian facilities.   
b. Because this condition of approval requires discretionary judgement and is not 
exclusively administrative in nature, and because resolution of this condition may require 
substantive changes to the CDP, a compliance public hearing with the Planning Board shall 
be held to confirm resolution of the items contained in this condition of approval. Public 
notice for said compliance hearing shall be in accordance with the statutory requirements of 
RSA 676:4(d)(1) and notification fees shall be paid by the applicant 
5. Prior to final approval, and as required by Section 12.09 Electronic Submission of the 
Subdivision Regulations, digital information from the plat shall be provided to the City Engineer 
for incorporation into the City of Concord Geographic Information (GIS) and tax maps. 
6. Following the compliance public hearing required by precedent condition 4.b above, and 
upon notification from the Planning Division that the project complies with the precedent 
conditions, Zoning Ordinance, and Subdivision Regulations, the applicant shall deliver to the 
Planning Division for signature by the Chair and Clerk three full size plan sets that contain the 
signature and seal of the appropriate licensed professionals as required by the Subdivision 
Regulations.   
(b) Subsequent Conditions 
1. This approval notwithstanding, the applicant is responsible for full knowledge of, and 
compliance with, the municipal code, Subdivision Regulations, and Concord Construction 
Standards and Details for the project, unless a variance, waiver, or conditional use permit is 
granted. 
2. Per Section 18.06 Issuance of a Decision, all subsequent subdivision and site plan 
approvals shall be in accordance with the approved comprehensive development plan. 
3. This CDP approval is binding regarding the proposed land uses, general lot configuration, 
general density, and primary circulation; however, specific site details are non-binding, provided 
they align with the general configuration and intent of the CDP, and remain subject to subsequent 
subdivision and site plan approval. 
4. This CDP approval does not authorize the applicant or owner to undertake any 
construction related to the proposed improvements.  The applicant or owner must subsequently 
file and obtain subdivision approval for the platting of lots and site plan approvals for the 
development of improvements as proposed within the CDP. All subsequent applications shall be 
in compliance with applicable City of Concord Zoning Ordinances, Site Plan Regulations, and 
Subdivision Regulations, as well as any necessary approvals as may be required by NHDOT for 
improvements on state-controlled roadways. Approval of the CDP does not remove or release the 
applicant or owner from any such land use requirement. 
5. Conditional approval of this CDP shall allow any related subdivision, site plan, or 
conditional use permit application to be determined complete (as it relates to the CDP being a 
component of an application’s determination of completeness, understanding that all other 
regulatory requirements as necessary under RSA 676:4 and the relevant regulations must be 
satisfied); however, final approval of this CDP is required as a prerequisite of any subsequent 
land use permit application (subdivision, site plan, conditional use permit, or any other local land 
use permit) being granted final approval by the Planning Board.
City of Concord Planning Board 
November 2, 2026 - Draft 
 Minutes 
 
 
6 
 
 
6. The full and final Traffic Impact Analysis must be completed, and approved by the City 
Engineer and NH Department of Transportation, including any applicable related permitting 
(NHDOT Driveway and any others as applicable), prior to the final approval (signature by the 
Chair and Clerk) of any subsequent site plan application for development contemplated by this 
CDP.  Because of the applicant’s proposed construction sequencing, the full final traffic impact 
analysis shall be utilized for the subsequent site plan applications, and their conditions of 
approval shall likewise be tied to the final approval of the full comprehensive traffic impact 
analysis by both the City and NHDOT. 
7. All required off-site transportation improvements, identified as part of the final Traffic 
Impact Analysis, as described in Subsequent condition 6, shall be completed prior to the issuance 
of any certificates of occupancy required for the development of the site.  This condition shall 
also be applied to all forthcoming site plan applications associated with the CDP. 
8. The City shall not issue any certificates of occupancy required for the development until 
the Heights Sewer Project (CIP 275, Pump Station, and CIP 91, Sewer Main) are completed by 
the City. This condition shall also be applied to all forthcoming site plan applications associated 
with the CDP. 
 
5.  Master Plan Workshop Items  
 
5A. Consideration of Public Safety Advisory Board Master Plan Request 
 Mr. Walsh stated there was a memo that was provided by the Public Safety Advisory Board to City 
Council and Planning Board. Mr. Walsh noted there are three requests at the bottom of the report. The 
master plan will discuss public safety to a certain extent for fire service. They will do our best to try 
and do some projections on future needs. This was sent to Planning Board at the direction of City 
Council.  
 
Chair Woodfin asked if the letter is on behalf of the Public Safety Advisory Board which is 
represented as a police department board or the fire department.  
 
Mr. Walsh stated public safety dips into the fire department and not sure why it is on the police 
department letterhead. 
 
Chair Woodfin asked what is the action for the Board to take on this letter.  
 
Mr. Walsh stated it is up to the Board accepting the report and if there is any response they wish to 
provide.  
 
Chair Woodfin asked about item two “include an analysis coordinating anticipated residential and 
commercial growth with future public-safety needs, including personnel, apparatus, facilities, 
potential future facility locations, service capacity, response volumes, and projected demand; and” 
are they asking the Board to do that as a part of the master plan process.  
 
Mr. Walsh cannot speak for the Public Safety Advisory Board. The master plan will have a higher 
level looking at long term planning needs.
City of Concord Planning Board 
November 2, 2026 - Draft 
 Minutes 
 
 
7 
 
 
Chair Woodfin asked about item three “Include the Public Safety Advisory Board in the Master 
Plan’s planning and community engagement process” 
 
On a motion made by Chair Woodfin, seconded by Member Councilor Todd, the Board voted 9-0-0 
to accept the report as submitted. 
 
5B. Appointment of Master Plan Advisory Subcommittee 
Mr. Walsh stated back in June the Planning Board decided to have an advisory subcommittee 
appointed for the master plan process. The Board decided to have a subcommittee in July and August. 
The decision was made to have a 15-member subcommittee with six members of the Planning Board, 
one member from Conservation Commission, Economic Development Advisory Committee, Energy 
& Environment Committee, Heritage Commission, Recreations and Parks Advisory Committee, 
Transportation Policy Advisory Committee and three members of the public. In August there was a 
letter sent to those six boards and commissions asking for a primary representative to be nominated 
and an alternate. At that time, they also sent a letter to the public for a letter of interest. The Board can 
now formally appoint the group to move forward. The committee will meet four times to advise on 
key issues to address.  
 
On a motion made by Chair Woodfin, seconded by Councilor Todd, the Board voted 9-0-0 to 
nominate Planning Board Members•Amanda Savage •Paige Wilbur•Rich Woodfin •Dina 
Condodemetraky •Leon LaFreniere•Matt Hicks; Conservation Commission Nominations •Primary: 
Tracey Lesser •Alternate: Bruce Currie; Energy & Environment Committee Nominations •Primary: 
City Councilor Mark Davie•Alternate: None; Economic Development Advisory Committee 
Nominations•Primary:  Alex Stoyle•Alternate: Ari Pollack; Heritage Commission Nominations 
•Primary: Althea Barton•Alternate: Carol Durgy Brooks; Transportation Advisory Policy Committee 
Nominations •Primary: Craig Tufts•Alternate: Ian McGregor; Recreation Parks Advisory Committee 
Nominations •Primary: Rob Kleiner •Alternate: Sarah Beauregard. 
 
On a motion made by Chair Woodfin, seconded by Member Condodemetraky, the Board voted 9-0-0 
to nominate Noah Hodgetts, Chris Carley and Elizabeth Immen.  
 
5C. Visioning Open House Debrief 
Mr. Walsh noted there were 115 people that signed the sign in sheet. There might have been more 
like a 150 people at the session. They received 64 comment cards, 630 post-it notes and 728 dot 
stickers on the boards. Utile is working on the comments and themes.  
 
Chair Woodfin stated heard from several people it was well done and attended.  
 
Councilor Todd stated the success was due to city staff and the engagement with the public.  
 
Mr. Walsh stated staff had fun doing it. 
 
5D. NH Listens and Offer for additional youth focused event 
Mr. Walsh stated on September 19th NH Listens was at the event with a youth engagement section. 
NH Listens offered if the Board wishes to have a youth specific event and will work with the city.
City of Concord Planning Board 
November 2, 2026 - Draft 
 Minutes 
 
 
8 
 
 
Chair Woodfin asked if this is a Utile event.  
 
Mr. Walsh stated they did not contemplate with the scope of the work in the contract for Utile. It is up 
to the Board if they want to take up on the offer. 
 
Member Condodemetraky thought this would be a good thing.  
 
Chair Woodfin is in favor.  
 
The consensus of the Board was to move forward with an event with NH Listens. 
 
5E. Upcoming Public Engagement: Strategy for 6 Neighborhood / Village Forums 
 
Mr. Walsh stated there will be a total of six neighborhood / village forums as planned as part of the 
Master Plan Update, focused on: East Concord, the Heights, the South-End, West-end/North-
End/Downtown; West Concord, and Penacook. These events are tentatively scheduled to take place 
this coming Winter. Does the Board want to do on a week night or a Saturday. If you did a Saturday 
would the Board be interested in two per day or a Friday night and Saturday morning. There was also 
discussion on locations for the meetings based on the location.   
 
Chair Woodfin does not want two per day. 
 
Councilor Todd suggested to have one evening session and a weekend session.  
 
Mr. Walsh stated it is about minimizing their travel. Mr. Walsh asked if Friday night or Saturday 
morning would work.  
 
The consensus of the Board was to have the meetings on a Friday night and a Saturday morning.  
 
Adjournment 
On a motion made by Member Condodemetraky, seconded by Member Hicks, the Board voted 9-0-0 to 
adjourn the meeting at 7:39 p.m.  
 
The next regular meeting is Wednesday, November 18, 2026, at 7:00 p.m.
